title: Pegasus Payments - Postmortem Incident Followup
summary: Follow-up to the June 18 incident where Pegasus saw elevated token latencies and intermittent 503s during a nightly batch. We reviewed the postmortem draft, aligned on root cause (KV-cache eviction + autoscaler misconfiguration + degraded NFS), agreed on mitigations, and committed to a short pilot of caching and autoscaler tweaks. Next steps include logs/benchmark handoff, security doc delivery, and a follow-up on July 2 for verification.
next_steps: Redwood to send final postmortem doc and timeline (Samir) by 2026-06-26
SE to share repro logs and benchmark scripts (Elena) by 2026-06-28
Pegasus to run internal canary of cache tweak over weekend and report results by 2026-06-30
action_items: Elena Martinez: Run load repro against staging, capture KV cache metrics and share logs (due 2026-06-28)
Aisha Rahman: Provide mounts/ops details and NFS metrics for 2026-06-18 window (due 2026-06-26)
Samir Patel: Share final postmortem doc, proposed rollback/fallback playbook, and security attachments (SOC2 summary, audit logs) (due 2026-06-26)
Tom Garcia: Approve a 48-hour pilot of increased cache retention and autoscaler threshold change (decision due 2026-06-27)
meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-25 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes | Recording: available in Fireflies
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, we're doing a follow up on the Pegasus incident postmortem. Ill hand over to Priya to, uh, kick off.
[00:23] Priya: yeah thanks Samir, hi Michael, Aisha, Tom, appreciate the time. The goal here is to align on root cause, lock down mitigations and confirm next steps. Well keep it tight, about 45-60 minutes.
[00:38] Michael: thanks, yeah we want to make sure we can run our nightly batches without the spike in latencies, that caused downstream payments delays.
[00:45] Aisha: just to add, engineers saw a mix of 503s and 30-60s spikes, mostly between 02:10 and 02:45 UTC, and it correlated with our large tokenized job kickoff.
[01:05] Elena: quick recap from our side, root cause draft shows three compounding issues: the KV cache eviction due to low memory under high concurrency, the autoscaler policy had too low of a threshold so new instances didn't spin up quickly, and we observed NFS latency that exacerbated model load times.
[01:28] Tom: the NFS note is new to us, can you explain that a bit?
[01:35] Elena: sure, while the model weights are mostly local on GPU nodes, there's metadata and some sharded checkpoints on your NFS volume, and during the peak we saw read ops queue. The transcription of metrics may show as "mount slow" in the logs.
[01:58] Michael: ok that aligns with what Aisha saw. Wed thought it was a pure autoscale problem initially.
[02:12] Samir: and to be clear, the KV cache eviction was triggered because the cache retention config was set to a conservative value to save mem for multi-tenant, so during the burst a lot of prefixes were evicted and had to be recomputed which added 100s of ms per request and then caused more load.
[02:39] Aisha: yeah and then the autoscaler was configured with a 120s cool down, so instances weren't added quick enough.
[02:52] Elena: exactly, combined failure mode. Also there was a fallback mapping misconfig where the fallback model was a larger variant, which made cold starts heavier — that was a config mismatch in the rollout policy.
[03:12] Tom: ouch that seems backwards.
[03:17] Samir: agreed, we pointed that out in the draft. Were proposing three immediate mitigations: increase cache retention window for Pegasus' dedicated pool, lower autoscaler threshold and cool down for bursty jobs, and update fallback mapping to use a lighter-compatible model variant.
[03:41] Michael: how risky is increasing the cache retention? Could that blow memory and cause other evictions?
[03:50] Elena: good question. For your dedicated pool we can incrementally bump retention and monitor, we have a knob that sets per-tenant cache budget. We'll recommend a staged rollout: +25% for 48 hours, measure cache hit rate and memory pressure. If we see swap or OOM signals, roll back.
[04:14] Aisha: and the autoscaler change, what number are you thinking?
[04:20] Elena: lower the CPU/utilization trigger from 70% to 50% for this class of jobs and reduce cool down from 120s to 30s. That should spin up nodes faster. We can also provision a short burst capacity that keeps a warm node pool during known nightly windows.
[04:38] Tom: the warm node option sounds good but might cost more. Can we estimate cost impact?
[04:45] Samir: yes, we'll run a quick cost delta. Expect maybe ~8-12% increase during the window; we'll share an exact spreadsheet.
[04:58] Michael: and about the fallback mapping being the wrong model, how did that slip through?
[05:05] Elena: seems like a rollout artifact: the canary config pointed to the standard variant instead of a tiny/quantized variant in the model catalog. We're adding a pre-flight check to the rollout pipeline to assert fallback sizes.
[05:25] Priya: ok let's pivot to compliance questions from your security team that Aisha shared earlier. They wanted to confirm audit logs and SSO traces for the period?
[05:36] Aisha: yes we need retained audit logs for the actions around the deployment that night, and confirm that KMS keys were used for model artifacts and that logs show service accounts.
[05:48] Samir: well attach the SOC2 summary and a slice of audit logs for the timeframe; note that for Private customers we can provide additional KMS proof. For hosted we provide per-request metadata and can extract service account traces.
[06:05] Michael: will those logs expose any PII? We need assurances.
[06:10] Samir: no PII in logs, we redact payloads and only include metadata for ops. We'll include our retention policy doc.
[06:20] Tom: can you also confirm the fallback policy and the new pre-flight check are part of your CI job? We want a single source of truth.
[06:29] Elena: yes were adding a pre-deploy validator in the model rollout pipeline; it will assert that fallback mapping points to a compatible variant and will fail the rollout if not.
[06:40] Aisha: great. On the NFS piece, ops found spikes in dentry lookup times in the kernel, looks like your node images were contending on a shared mount in that AZ.
[06:58] Samir: that suggests a host-level ops tune or moving metadata to local ephemeral SSD could help. We can recommend moving model metadata shards onto local disks for faster reads.
[07:12] Michael: what about the timeline for fixes? Wed prefer not to patch in prod without a canary.
[07:18] Samir: agreed. plan: 1) quick config changes (cache retention + autoscaler tweak) as a pilot in staging this week, 2) Pegasus to run nightly canary over weekend, 3) if green, roll to prod with 2-hour canary window.
[07:35] Elena: well prepare the patch as a feature flag so you can toggle easily.
[07:42] Tom: and rollback plan?
[07:44] Elena: rollback is reverting the retention to previous value and restoring autoscaler thresholds, plus fallback mapping rollback. Well provide runbook steps in the postmortem doc.
[07:56] Michael: sounds good. Regarding the pilot, what metrics should we watch?
[08:02] Elena: cache hit rate, 99th percentile response latency, model cold start time, number of scaling events, and NFS read latency. We'll provide dashboards.
[08:17] Aisha: can you also include KV cache eviction traces?
[08:21] Elena: yes, will include KV cache eviction counts and prefix miss rates.
[08:26] Samir: quick note on cost: if you opt for warm nodes, well show a cost table and also a hybrid option where we only warm a single lightweight CPU node to keep metadata hot.
[08:40] Tom: any impact to SLOs if we change autoscaler?
[08:43] Elena: the SLOs should improve for latency, but throughput SLO might dip if we saturate warm nodes; thats why we'll do a short pilot.
[08:55] Michael: okay let's go through the postmortem doc section by section. Samir you flagged the timeline?
[09:01] Samir: timeline: 02:06 first error spike, 02:10 heavy token job kicked off, 02:12 cache miss spike, 02:15 autoscaler still in cool down, 02:22 first 503s observed, 02:40 gradual recovery as jobs finished and cache warmed. We have logs attached.
[09:26] Priya: anything to add from your side, Aisha?
[09:29] Aisha: just that the NFS ops spike persisted longer than expected, about 25 minutes. That lines up with the latency plateau in the graphs.
[09:40] Tom: ok root cause statement?
[09:42] Elena: root cause: concurrent large tokenized job caused cache pressure and evictions; autoscaler cooldown prevented timely capacity addition; NFS metadata read latency increased model load times; fallback config used a heavier variant—these combined led to high latencies and some 503s.
[10:03] Michael: mitigation priorities?
[10:06] Samir: 1) cache retention increase & cache budget for your tenant, 2) autoscaler tweak and warm node option, 3) fallback mapping pre-flight checks, 4) move critical metadata to local ephemeral storage or tune NFS.
[10:20] Elena: technical note: well also add a short circuit for long-tail prefix recompute — if recompute time > X we serve degraded but fast response. That reduces spike amplification.
[10:34] Aisha: what about instrumentation? we need clear signal we can alert on.
[10:38] Elena: were adding an alert for KV eviction rate > threshold and a combined alert for cache-miss-rate + deploy events during window.
[10:49] Michael: can you share those alert threshold suggestions?
[10:52] Elena: yes, in the doc. typical starting point: kv_eviction_rate > 1000/min or prefix_miss_rate > 5% triggers ops runbook.
[11:05] Tom: ok let's talk about verification. What does "green" look like for the pilot?
[11:09] Elena: reduction in 99p latency by >= 40% in the nightly window, cache hit rate > 85% and zero 5xx.
[11:19] Priya: timeline recap — Samir will send final postmortem, Elena will send repro and dashboards, Pegasus runs canary, and then we meet July 2.
[11:31] Michael: quick security question: will the audit logs include any API keys?
[11:36] Samir: no, keys are redacted, logs show request IDs, service accounts and timestamps.
[11:45] Aisha: one more ops question: after increasing retention, how do we ensure we don't evict other tenants?
[11:51] Elena: were scoped per-tenant budgets in your Dedicated pool, we can raise only for Pegasus and not affect others.
[12:02] Tom: good. Any other blockers?
[12:05] Michael: just timeline — we need the doc by tomorrow to sign off on pilot.
[12:09] Samir: well get the final doc and playbook to you by EOD tomorrow.
[12:15] Priya: ok wrapping up, action items are recorded, well post the recording and docs into the shared channel.
[12:23] Elena: Ill start repro runs now and share logs.
[12:27] Aisha: Ill pull NFS metrics and share the dentry timing info.
[12:31] Tom: thanks everyone.
[12:34] Michael: thanks.
[12:36] Samir: thanks all, well follow up with the postmortem and next steps.
[12:42] Priya: end.
